email.subject1: a signal play for dbt Labs
email.body1:
Rowan, saw dbt Labs just merged with Fivetran to build data infrastructure for agents.

A merger of that size opens up far more accounts in your New England territory than reps can cover while the combined motion settles, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for dbt Labs off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Rowan, quick follow-up for dbt Labs.

Post-merger, pipeline expectations on a territory usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your New England territory needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Rowan, last bit of proof for dbt Labs.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other data-infra teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Rowan, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling territory pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority through the integration, no problem at all. Post-merger stretches are their own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a data-platform motion? I'll tailor it to dbt Labs either way.
